answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs hence has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the timber hash is checked against the terrace checkpoint at intake, the relic audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. So the marginal impostor costs more than the marginal honest participant earns in 3 epochs. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
